Folks — added detailed sizing assumptions below so the team has a concrete starting point. Short summary first, details after.

Summary (pilot -> initial commit):
- Eval (pilot) target: 5–7 qps sustained across test window -> recommend 4 x H100 for Private eval, 6 x H100 reserved for Dedicated pilot to allow higher concurrency/burst.
- Committed pool for GA: 12 x H100 (~sustained 40–50 qps depending on batching) or equivalent A100-80GB quantized configs to balance cost.
- Lead times: vendor procurement and rack allocation — 8–12 weeks typical for high-demand SKUs; 4–6 weeks for standard availability depending on region.

Assumptions used in estimate:
- Model: L2-70B (dense) at fp16/8-bit quantized path
- Sequence length: average 512 tokens per request, peak 1024
- Average latency target: p95 < 800ms at target qps
- Batching: continuous batching with avg batch size 8–12 for cost efficiency

Sizing table (rough):
- Private eval: 4 x H100 (pilot) — allows isolated testing and kernel tuning
- Dedicated pilot: 6 x H100 — headroom for external demos and burst
- Committed Dedicated pool (post-contract): 12–16 x H100 or 24 x A100-80GB quantized (depends on cost tradeoffs)

Lead-time notes:
- If you want guaranteed Dedicated capacity locked in, we need a signed commit + configuration 10–12 weeks prior to desired start of sustained traffic.
- Private (on-prem) packaging and validation can be parallelized; if Acme controls hardware ordering we can accelerate to 3–5 weeks for packaging + software install once hardware is on-site.

Fallbacks and recommendations
- Start with a small reserved pilot and use our burst pool until committed hardware is provisioned.
- We can run an aggressive caching strategy during eval to reduce the committed pool needs (prefix caching + KV cache).

Attaching the csv with scenario numbers used for the math. Happy to walk through numbers on the call.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel — quick note on eval gating so we all align on what "success" looks like:

Eval duration: 3 weeks (as proposed) with two phases — functional / correctness (week 1) then load & perf (weeks 2–3).
Gating criteria (examples):
- Quality: pass A/B similarity against baseline on 3 canonical prompts (90%+ parity)
- Latency: p95 < 800ms across the 3-week perf window
- Stability: no more than 2 incidents affecting >10% of requests during the perf phase
- Ops: observed KV-cache hit-rate > 30% for repeated prefixes (if we enable caching)

Data & artifacts we need from Acme:
- Canonical prompt set (10–50 prompts)
- Representative traffic profile (qps, %peak, typical sequence lengths)
- List of third-party connectors to be tested (if any)

If we hit those gates we’ll sign off on the sizing shown by Karthik and move to commit planning. We can also add a short synthetic stress test to validate burst behavior.

— Soojin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
